gap: No result ChatGPT got gives power figures behind the heated-chamber claims. Every rival treats QIDI's 65 °C as equal to Bambu's 65 °C. In fact the QIDI Max4 has a 500 W chamber heater for 51.7 L, about 9.7 W per litre. The smaller QIDI Plus5 has 550 W for 30.7 L, about 17.9 W per litre. The Bambu H2S is limited to 1,170 W maximum on 110 V, against 2,050 W on 220 V. The Prusa CORE One L/L+ has no chamber heater: it reaches its 60 °C with bed heat and fans.
standout_why: I read three pages ChatGPT cited. desktop3dprinters.us/lists/chamber-temperature-specs gives max chamber °C and marks each printer active or passive, but it states that it lists no heater wattage. It has no power or voltage data. desktop3dprinters.us/lists/large-enclosed-3d-printers gives volume in litres, chamber °C and filtration, with no heater wattage and no 110 V vs 220 V figures. It already says the Prusa L+ reaches 60 °C with fans moving air across the heated bed, so that part is not new. The creativebloq.com guide was truncated when I fetched it, so I could not check it. I did not open the uncited findmy3dprinter, scrc, firstlayerlab or speakcad pages because I ran out of tool calls. On the pages I read, no rival puts the heater's power next to the size of the chamber it heats, and none mentions the H2S power limit on 110 V. This is new and useful for a US buyer. It does not decide the pick alone, because Bambu does not publish a separate H2S heater wattage and I found no measured chamber heat-up times.
decides: For the 'largest practical' pick, it qualifies the QIDI Max4 rather than ruling it out. It is the biggest chamber in ChatGPT's list, but its heater has about half the power per litre of the Plus5, so expect slower warm-up or weaker heat holding for ABS/ASA/PC near 65 °C. A buyer who mostly prints engineering materials is better served by the Plus5's heater-to-volume ratio. For the H2S, US shoppers should know the printer is limited to 1,170 W maximum on 110 V, about 57% of its 2,050 W maximum on 220 V. The Prusa CORE One L+ has no chamber heater. Its 'active' 60 °C comes from bed-heat convection (about 630 W total while preheating), so it is not equivalent to the dedicated-heater machines.

findings.label: Chamber heater watts per litre of build volume
findings.note: 500 W ÷ (390 × 390 × 340 mm = 51.7 L) = 9.67 W/L. Build volume is for the printable area, not the whole enclosure air volume, so use this only to compare models.

findings.note: 550 W ÷ (320 × 320 × 300 mm = 30.7 L) = 17.9 W/L. That is about 1.85× the Max4's figure, although both are rated 'up to 65 °C'.
